children.prompt: Using a ruler and compasses only, construct an isosceles triangle $ABC$ in which the angle $\angle ACB$ is a right angle.

answer.short:
Construct perpendiculars to $AB$ at $A$ and $B$ on the same side of $AB$. Bisect both right angles; their bisectors meet at $C$.

The base angles are both $45^\circ$, so $AC=BC$ and $\angle ACB=90^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Extend $AB$ beyond both endpoints. At each endpoint, mark two equally distant points on the extended line using a compass. From each pair, draw equal-radius intersecting arcs above $AB$ and join the intersection to the endpoint. This constructs perpendiculars at $A$ and $B$ on the same side of $AB$.

Bisect the right angle at each endpoint using the compass angle-bisection construction. Label the intersection of the bisectors $C$ and draw $AC$ and $BC$. Retain the construction arcs.

Both base angles are $45^\circ$, so the opposite sides $AC$ and $BC$ are equal. By the angle sum of a triangle,
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-45^\circ-45^\circ\\\angle ACB&=90^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Thus $ABC$ is an isosceles triangle with a right angle at $C$.
